evidence.label: Strong with supervision
evidence.meaning: Trials support it as part of supervised therapy. Home practice alone is not proven.

evidence.label: Moderate
evidence.meaning: Small or mixed trials point to a real effect.

evidence.label: Limited
evidence.meaning: Early studies only, or tested only as part of a wider programme.

evidence.label: Unproven
evidence.meaning: No trial shows a benefit. Included for variety, warm-up or tracking.

evidence.label: Measures only
evidence.meaning: A test or check. It measures; it does not treat.

mechanisms.label: Two-eye video
mechanisms.basis: In one trial children gained 1.8 lines in 12 weeks, against 0.8 with glasses alone. In other trials two-eye video did about as well as patching.

mechanisms.label: Two-eye balanced play
mechanisms.basis: Same mechanism as the video trials. Game trials were mixed and tracked how much children played.

mechanisms.label: Vergence training
mechanisms.basis: With weekly supervised sessions, 73% of children succeeded or improved. Adults gained 17 prism dioptres of reserve.

mechanisms.label: Depth training
mechanisms.basis: In pooled adult studies, about a third of those with some depth vision improved it markedly.

mechanisms.label: Anti-suppression
mechanisms.basis: Supervised therapy improved squint control by 0.9 points on a 5-point scale.

mechanisms.label: Perceptual learning
mechanisms.basis: In pooled studies adults gained about 1.7 lines on the letter chart.

mechanisms.label: Habit coaching
mechanisms.basis: Enforced breaks eased strain scores in two weeks. Blink training improved dry-eye scores at 30 days.

mechanisms.label: Scanning training
mechanisms.basis: Search into the blind side sped up by 24% after 800 trials of web training.

mechanisms.label: Eye-movement play
mechanisms.basis: No trial shows a benefit in healthy eyes.

mechanisms.label: Check in game form
mechanisms.basis: Home acuity tests agree with clinic charts to within one line.

mechanisms.label: Outdoor light
mechanisms.basis: An extra 40 minutes outdoors a day cut myopia onset from 39.5% to 30.4% over three years.

mechanisms.label: Patching support
mechanisms.basis: Patching is standard care, and two hours a day worked as well as six.

mechanisms.label: Glasses first
mechanisms.basis: Glasses alone gained 2.9 lines on average and resolved lazy eye in 27% of children.

mechanisms.label: Focus flexibility
mechanisms.basis: Part of supervised therapy protocols. Not tested alone.

mechanisms.label: Reading distance
mechanisms.basis: Supports the outdoor habit. Not tested alone as a treatment.

mechanisms.label: Reading practice
mechanisms.basis: Related to search training. Smaller evidence base.

mechanisms.label: Home monitoring
mechanisms.basis: Cleared home tests of this kind exist. Results are compared with the user's own baseline.

mechanisms.label: Reminders
mechanisms.basis: In one trial, reminders raised the share of doses taken from 53% to 64%.

mechanisms.label: Supervised recovery
mechanisms.basis: After concussion, 79% improved with six weeks of supervised therapy, against 13% of those waiting.

mechanisms.label: Atropine support
mechanisms.basis: In trials, atropine drops worked as well as daily patching for moderate lazy eye.

games.name: Lantern Run
games.play: Run and jump through a night market. The runner and coins show to the weaker eye, the obstacles to the stronger eye.
games.purpose: Makes the weaker eye lead while both eyes work together

games.name: Firefly Catch
games.play: Tap the fireflies and leave the moths. Fireflies show only to the weaker eye.
games.purpose: Picking out weak-eye targets in clutter

games.name: Maze of Two Lights
games.play: Roll a ball through a maze. The ball belongs to the weaker eye, the walls to the stronger eye.

games.name: Tunnel Glide
games.play: Fly through rings that drift apart. Keep each ring single to pass.

games.name: Depth Darts
games.play: Throw at the target that floats nearest.

games.name: Comet Trail
games.play: Keep a ring on a drifting comet with a finger or the remote.

games.name: Spot Jump
games.play: Hit targets that appear left and right in sequence.

games.name: Blink Garden
games.play: Plants grow with every full blink the camera sees.
games.for: Screen strain and dry eye · ages 8+ · level 0

games.name: Far Window
games.play: A 20-second break. Find three far-off things; the camera confirms the eyes left the screen.

games.name: E Safari
games.play: Point the way the animal tracks face. The tracks shrink until the child can no longer tell.
games.gear: Patch for one eye at a time

games.name: Sky Spotter
games.play: An outdoor scavenger hunt. Find far-off things in daylight and log them on the phone.

exercises.name: Brock String
exercises.how: Hold a string with three beads to the nose. Look from bead to bead and see the strings cross at each one.
exercises.purpose: Feeling and controlling where the eyes aim

exercises.name: Target Push-ups
exercises.how: Bring a small letter slowly toward the nose and keep it single. Stop when it doubles, then back off.

exercises.name: Barrel Card
exercises.how: Hold the card on the nose and converge on each of three barrels in turn.

exercises.name: Dot Card
exercises.how: Hold a line of dots at the nose and walk the eyes from the far dot to the near one.

exercises.name: Lifesaver Card
exercises.how: Cross the eyes until two rings merge into a third ring that looks clear and raised.

exercises.name: Near-Far Jumps
exercises.how: Switch gaze between a thumb at arm's length and a letter across the room.

exercises.name: Screen Vergence Ramp
exercises.how: A target on screen slowly drifts apart. Hold it single as long as possible.

exercises.name: Screen Vergence Steps
exercises.how: The demand changes in sudden steps. Regain a single image after each one.

exercises.name: Flip Switch
exercises.how: Alternate converge and diverge demand and count the flips per minute.

exercises.name: Long Hold
exercises.how: Hold a high demand for two minutes without doubling.
exercises.purpose: Slow adaptation of the vergence system

exercises.name: Near-Far Focus Rock
exercises.how: Read a letter chart at 3 m, then a card at 40 cm, back and forth.
exercises.for: Focusing problems with convergence insufficiency · ages 8+

exercises.name: One-Eye Focus Rock
exercises.how: The same near-far reading with one eye covered, then the other.

exercises.name: Cinema Session
exercises.how: Watch a show in the two-eye player. The weaker eye gets full contrast, the stronger eye reduced contrast.
exercises.dose: 60 min a day in chapters, 6 days a week

exercises.name: Patch-Time Detail Tasks
exercises.how: Tracing, dot-to-dot and bead threading on the tablet while the patch is on.
exercises.purpose: Keeps the patch on and the weaker eye working
exercises.dose: As prescribed, often 2 h a day

exercises.name: Glasses-First Log
exercises.how: Wear the new glasses all day, log it, and check acuity every five weeks.
exercises.purpose: Lets glasses do their part before any training

exercises.name: Contrast Ladder
exercises.how: Find faint stripes with the weaker eye as the contrast steps down.

exercises.name: Crowding Drill
exercises.how: Read the middle letter as its neighbours close in.

exercises.name: Line-Up Drill
exercises.how: Nudge one line until it sits exactly under another.

exercises.name: See Both Lights
exercises.how: Look at a small light through the glasses and keep both the red and the cyan image visible.
exercises.purpose: Awareness of both eyes at once

exercises.name: Distance Fusion Hold
exercises.how: Hold a fused target on the TV at 3 m as the demand rises.

exercises.name: Look-Away Break
exercises.how: Every 20 minutes look at something 6 m away for 20 seconds.

exercises.name: Full-Blink Drill
exercises.how: Close gently, pause, squeeze lightly, open. Ten times.
exercises.purpose: Complete blinks that spread the tear film

exercises.name: Distance Reset
exercises.how: The camera measures working distance and coaches it back to arm's length.

exercises.name: Desk Set-up Check
exercises.how: Guided check of screen height, glare and brightness against the room.
exercises.purpose: A screen that is easy on the eyes

exercises.name: Outdoor Light Time
exercises.how: Reach the daily daylight goal, logged by phone or watch.
exercises.purpose: Slows the onset of short sight

exercises.name: Arm's-Length Reading
exercises.how: The tablet camera nudges a child who leans in too close.

exercises.name: Blind-Side Sweeps
exercises.how: Make large, deliberate eye sweeps into the blind side to find each target.
exercises.purpose: Finding things on the missing side

exercises.name: Guided Line Reading
exercises.how: Read scrolling text with a guide that marks the start and end of each line.

exercises.name: Weekly Grid Check
exercises.how: Cover one eye and look at a grid. Mark any bent or missing lines.
exercises.purpose: Catching change at the centre of vision

exercises.name: Drop Reminder Routine
exercises.how: A reminder at drop time, a one-tap log, and a weekly tally.

exercises.name: Bead Slide
exercises.how: Slide one bead along the string toward the nose and keep the strings crossing at the bead.

exercises.name: Stereogram Pairs
exercises.how: Fuse two side-by-side pictures into a third that appears in depth, first by crossing the eyes, then by relaxing them.
exercises.purpose: Fusion without glasses, in both directions

exercises.name: Screen Diverge Ramp
exercises.how: A target drifts the other way, so the eyes must relax outward to keep it single.

exercises.name: Reading Under Demand
exercises.how: Read a short passage while the screen holds a set convergence demand.
exercises.purpose: Carrying the skill into real reading

exercises.name: Therapy Homework Plan
exercises.how: The home half of supervised therapy: the drills the therapist set that week, timed and logged.
exercises.purpose: Doing the home practice the trials required
exercises.dose: 15 min a day, 5 days a week, 12 weeks

exercises.name: Three-Chapter Cinema Plan
exercises.how: Split the daily hour into three 20-minute sittings: after school, before dinner, before bed.
exercises.purpose: Fitting the full dose into a school day

exercises.name: Patch Wear Timer
exercises.how: Start the timer when the patch goes on. A sticker chart fills as the hours add up.

exercises.name: Bead Threading
exercises.how: Thread beads onto a string while the patch is on.
exercises.purpose: Close, fine work for the weaker eye
exercises.for: Children prescribed a patch · ages 3 to 8

exercises.name: Patch-On Ball Play
exercises.how: Roll, bounce and catch a ball with the patch on.

exercises.name: Atropine-Day Companion
exercises.how: A reminder on drop days, a one-tap log, and near-work games suited to drop days.

exercises.name: Glasses Check-in
exercises.how: A daily camera check that glasses are on, with a weekly wear score for the caregiver.

exercises.name: Class Outdoor Period
exercises.how: A school class adds one outdoor period a day and logs it as a squad.
exercises.purpose: Daylight time, delivered the way the trial did

exercises.name: Walk-to-School Log
exercises.how: Walk or cycle part of the school run and log the daylight minutes.
exercises.purpose: Daylight built into the school day

exercises.name: Weekend Outdoor Block
exercises.how: A planned outdoor block on each weekend day, logged as a family.
exercises.dose: 1 h or more each weekend day

exercises.name: Walk-In Target
exercises.how: Walk slowly toward a letter on the wall and keep it single and clear.
exercises.for: Vision problems after concussion · level 2, counsellor plan

exercises.name: Head-Turn Letter Hold
exercises.how: Keep a letter clear while turning the head slowly side to side.
exercises.for: Vision problems after concussion · level 2, counsellor plan

exercises.name: Near-Far with Movement
exercises.how: Switch focus between a near card and a far chart while stepping side to side.
exercises.for: Vision problems after concussion · level 2, counsellor plan

themes.name: Rewards only eyes can open
themes.what: Prizes that are tied to the skill being trained, so earning them and practising are the same act.

themes.name: Community without a feed
themes.what: Ways to belong that need no timeline, no followers and no scrolling.

themes.name: One shared purpose
themes.what: Things the whole community builds together, one session at a time.

themes.name: Rituals in the real world
themes.what: Fixed times and places that turn home practice into something people do together.

themes.name: Finishing well
themes.what: How a day ends and how a programme ends.

ideas.name: Fusion Mail
ideas.what: Notes from family and buddies are split between the eyes, half the letters to each. They can be read only when both eyes work together through the glasses.
ideas.why: A message from a grandparent pulls harder than points, and reading it is itself the practice.
ideas.isNew: The reward is physically locked to the skill being trained.

ideas.name: Locked Gallery
ideas.what: Trophy pictures drawn in finer depth steps and fainter contrast than the member can see today. Each becomes visible when their own test results reach it.
ideas.why: Progress turns into something seen. Effort trophies sit beside them for members who improve slowly.
ideas.isNew: Trophies that cannot be seen until vision improves.

ideas.name: First Depth Day
ideas.what: When the depth test first passes, the TV plays a short scene in real depth built from the member's own hero. The date is kept like a birthday.
ideas.why: Gaining depth is unforgettable. Neuroscientist Susan Barry gained it at 48 and described her steering wheel floating in front of the dashboard.
ideas.isNew: A celebration that could not have been seen the day before.

ideas.name: Draw Your Hero
ideas.what: A child's own drawing, photographed, becomes the weak-eye character in every game.
ideas.why: Children stay longer with something they made, and the hero travels with them from game to game.
ideas.isNew: The therapy image is authored by the child being treated.

ideas.name: Notes From Four Weeks Ahead
ideas.what: At each milestone a member leaves one tip for whoever reaches that week next, and receives the notes left by people who already passed it.
ideas.why: Advice from someone just ahead is easier to believe than advice from an expert, and nobody is compared with anybody.
ideas.isNew: A community with no feed, no followers and no scrolling.

ideas.name: Lend a Light
ideas.what: Streak savers exist only as gifts. Showing up earns lights that cannot be spent on oneself, only given to someone about to lose a streak.
ideas.why: Being rescued by a stranger, and rescuing one, binds people more than a badge does.
ideas.isNew: The only currency is generosity. It cannot be hoarded or bought.

ideas.name: Proof of Help
ideas.what: Standing comes from measured benefit: "42 people's results moved after trying your routine." There are no likes and no follower counts.
ideas.why: Status goes to the people who help, not the loudest.
ideas.isNew: Reputation computed from other people's test results.

ideas.name: Duet Streak
ideas.what: Two people in different generations keep one streak, such as a child's cinema hour and a grandparent's eye drops. It grows only when both do their part.
ideas.why: Each becomes the other's reason to show up, and eye care becomes a family matter.
ideas.isNew: One streak across two conditions and two generations.

ideas.name: Focus Wall
ideas.what: Each month a picture drawn by a child member starts out blurred. Every finished session anywhere sharpens one tile until the whole picture is in focus.
ideas.why: Each member's effort visibly counts toward something shared.
ideas.isNew: A collective goal that looks like the thing being treated.

ideas.name: Discovery Board
ideas.what: Members vote on the next question the pooled data should answer. When it is answered, everyone who took part is credited: "You helped find this."
ideas.why: Play becomes contribution. Sea Hero Quest reached 4.3 million players this way and fed dementia research.
ideas.isNew: Members choose the research questions and share the credit.

ideas.name: Travelling Glasses
ideas.what: Each pair of glasses carries a code and a logbook. A child who finishes passes the pair on, and the next child sees who wore it before them.
ideas.why: A new family starts with proof that others finished, and a graduate's last act is a gift.
ideas.isNew: The equipment carries the community's history.

ideas.name: Light the Map
ideas.what: A map lights up by pin code as families join. The first family in each pin code becomes its lamp-lighter and welcomes the next.
ideas.why: Growth becomes a local game, and a newcomer meets a neighbour first.
ideas.isNew: Founding status that can only be used to welcome someone.

ideas.name: Lights On Hour
ideas.what: One fixed hour a week when everyone practises at once, and the TV shows a lantern rising for every household online. A yearly festival falls on World Sight Day.
ideas.why: A shared appointment is easier to keep than a private one. parkrun runs free, volunteer-led weekly events at over 2,000 locations on the same idea.
ideas.isNew: Solitary home therapy becomes a weekly gathering.

ideas.name: Cinema Club
ideas.what: Volunteers host a weekly two-eye film hour at a school or library with one TV and a box of glasses.
ideas.why: Children without a TV at home can take part, and families meet in person.
ideas.isNew: The therapy room is a neighbourhood club night.
ideas.build: Small, a host kit and guide

ideas.name: Class Mission
ideas.what: The child with the patch receives a kit to run a five-minute glasses game for the whole class.
ideas.why: The patch stops being the odd thing out. In a small follow-up study, adults treated before school age recalled more victimisation by peers.
ideas.isNew: The child being treated holds the key to a game everyone wants to play.

ideas.name: Wish Jam
ideas.what: Developers and students build a game for one named child's wish, such as trains instead of blocks. The child tests it and names it.
ideas.why: Builders work harder for a real child than for a brief, and the library fills with games children asked for.
ideas.isNew: A game jam where every entry has a first player waiting.

ideas.name: Sunset Rule
ideas.what: The day's play closes when the dose is done. The screen shows a sunset and the Light ring invites the child outside.
ideas.why: Parents trust an app that ends itself. The league rewards finishing, never lingering.
ideas.isNew: A game designed to be put down.

ideas.name: Keeper Graduation
ideas.what: Finishing a programme ends with a ceremony on the TV, a printable journey book, and an invitation to become a keeper who welcomes one new family.
ideas.why: The end of treatment becomes the start of belonging.
ideas.isNew: Every graduate leaves one welcome behind.
